question: Second-generation oral antihistamines (e.g., cetirizine, loratadine) are the single most effective drug class for controlling the full spectrum of allergic rhinitis symptoms.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually false. While antihistamines are widely used, intranasal corticosteroids are the most effective monotherapy for allergic rhinitis. They suppress the entire inflammatory cascade (not just histamine), providing superior control of congestion, sneezing, rhinorrhoea, and nasal itch compared to antihistamines alone.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. Intranasal corticosteroids (e.g., fluticasone, mometasone) are the most effective single drug class for allergic rhinitis. They suppress the entire nasal inflammatory cascade — histamine, leukotrienes, prostaglandins, and cytokines — whereas oral antihistamines only block the histamine pathway, leaving congestion and other mediator-driven symptoms less well controlled.
